adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `uniqueGuests` in addGuests.handler.ts line 74 only filters against existing `booking.attendees` but does not deduplicate the input `guests` array itself. Looking at the code: `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter((guest) => !booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email) && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`. If a client sends `['a@b.com', 'a@b.com']`, both would pass this filter (neither is in existing attendees), resulting in duplicate attendee rows being created via `createMany`. While the UI dialog validates for uniqueness, the server-side schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` without uniqueness constraint, so a direct API call could bypass the UI validation.
